content: Replication check: the basic result, that people finish later than their own probability-weighted forecasts, has been reproduced many times with students, professionals and software projects. A review of four decades of time-prediction studies (Halkjelsvik & Jørgensen 2012) confirms frequent underestimation, but finds the direction depends on task length and elicitation format, with short tasks often overestimated. Roy, Christenfeld & McKenzie (2005) challenge Buehler et al.'s mechanism: people misremember how long past tasks took, rather than neglecting that history. The effect holds; the claim that people ignore their past is the contested part.
